title: Legislative districts of Zamboanga City
wikitext:
{{Short description|none}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Zamboanga City''' are the representations of the [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|highly urbanized city]] of [[Zamboanga City|Zamboanga]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The city is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] congressional districts. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mindanao and Sulu|Legislative district of Zamboanga|Legislative district of Zamboanga del Sur}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Zamboanga City were represented under the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] (1917–1935), [[Zamboanga (province)|Zamboanga Province]] (1935–1953), [[Zamboanga del Sur]] (1953–1972) and [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region IX]] (1978–1984). Having been re-classified as a [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|highly urbanized city]] on November 22, 1983, Zamboanga City was granted separate representation for the first time in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]], when it returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|one representative, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the city constituted a [[#Lone District (defunct)|lone congressional district]],{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 19, 2017}} and elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. The enactment of Republic Act No. 9269 on March 19, 2004 increased Zamboanga City's representation by reapportioning it into two congressional districts,{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 9260 - An Act Creating the Second Legislative District of the City of Zamboanga|url=https://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2004/ra_9269_2004.html|author=Congress of the Philippines|date=March 19, 2004|website=The LawPhil Project|access-date=November 26, 2017}} which began to elect their separate representatives in the [[2007 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2007 elections]].
